events.title: First cabaret songs published
events.label: 1926 · First cabaret songs
events.shortDescription: Kaper’s first Warsaw cabaret songs appear under the pseudonym Bruno Asper.
events.longDescription: Songs for Warsaw cabarets published under the pseudonym Bruno Asper (lyrics by Andrzej Włast).

events.title: Meeting Walter Jurmann
events.label: 1931 · Meeting Walter Jurmann
events.shortDescription: Kaper meets Walter Jurmann, launching the songwriting partnership that defines his European film career.
events.longDescription: Introduced by Fritz Rotter, marking the start of the Jurmann–Kaper duo. First joint project: “Die große Attraktion,” directed by Max Reichmann. Kaper composes the hit slow fox “Du warst mir ein Roman” for Richard Tauber.

events.title: Hollywood debut
events.label: 1935 · Hollywood debut
events.shortDescription: Kaper makes his Hollywood debut at MGM, contributing to Escapade and other major studio projects.
events.longDescription: First American score: "Escapade" (dir. Robert Z. Leonard) with William Powell and Luise Rainer. Press hails "Two New Composers" of Kiepura's European hits. Songs also for Marx Brothers' "A Night at the Opera" (with Ned Washington) and "Mutiny on the Bounty".
